The Schrykes now no longer share a single vision of what order is, and thus infighting will commence. Factions and wars, squabbling, and disagreement. Yet all those orderly, for the Schrykes still value order.

Phyra went to travel Gaea and search for the most prized creation by Umbralocht. In a tribe of Flora he saw something, a glimmer... A shiver around one of the Flora, as if the Flora was there and was not there at the same time. Phyra forced the Flora to teleport to one of the Heavy Planes. For the Heavy Planes were a harsh landscape and no god or mortal had yet stepped foot.

The creature looked aghast as the ground and sky around him had just vanished and reappeared. It was crushed to the ground by the enourmous gravity. "Hello" the air around the creature spoke. The creature now looked fearfull.

After a long boring interregation by Phyra, nothing special about the creature was revealed, it truly believed itself to be a Flora. The creature looked exhausted, fearfull yet still honest. All the begging, crying and pleading had had it's impact. But the shimmering and shifting of it's image didn't stop to the eyes of Phyra. Phyra was certain that this was a creation by Umbralocht.

Phyra used it's powers of order to dismantle the creature to it's very essence, to stack all of the bits and pieces it was created from back in the box they came from. He discovered that this was never even a real Flora to begin with, the creation was completely by the hand of Umbralocht. This pleased Phyra as he knew he had found the proper target for his grudge. Phyra stripped away the creatures soul and discovered it's values and essence piece by piece while he dismantled it to dust. He stripped away the creatures magic and discovered the workings of the shapeshifters power, this was actually very well done and he had to commend the obsessive side of Umbralocht for being thorough. Though he was certain the shapeshifting wasn't only by the hand of Umbralocht he couldn't quite figure out what the other power was.

Now there was a different creature on the ground, but still the honest and fearfull look remained, even with the soul stripped and it being an empty vessel. Phyra knew the creature hadn't done any wrong for it didn't know any better, it would never have known what it was until it transformed into this family eating nightmare.

Phyra continued to strip it's mind and the rest of his being.

When he was finished all he had left was the Dust of XOM. His very antithesis, the source of all chaos. Phyra pondered if Shamar, God of Preservation wasn't right all along, that Phyra was too soft to even allow life, to even allow change.

Phyra also had a small chuckle that Dreka would be mad at him for leaving nothing of the creature behind to go to the realm of death.

He crafted a small relic, a locket, to store the dust of XOM until he had a more permanent solution for the nasty stuff. At least now he didn't need to worry about having to touch it. What a vile stuff it was, it disgusted Phyra to the core of his being.

Armed with the knowledge of exactly what he was dealing with Phyra set out to invent a countermeasure so order could be restored by the mortals themselves. Phyra had little time for the qualms of mortals, that's what the Schrykes were for.

What is your preferred break in period before you deem a new firearm something worthy of carrying? It's never a good idea to take a brand new, or even used gun and start carrying it without actually having fired it. Even with reputable brands and companies it's always a good idea to run rounds through it, including the rounds you plan to carry, before you actually start to carry it.

For me, I usually try to run no less than 300 rounds of cheap FMJ through anything I intend to potentially carry to see if I have any failures or issues. Then it's on to a box of whatever ammo I want to carry, usually Hornady Critical Duty. When I go to the range I always take whatever pistols I sometimes carry in rotation and make sure to throw some lead downrange with them as well.

So, let's pretend you just bought a new gun today and it may replace your existing carry piece or become part of your rotation for carry. You just got home from your LGS and are headed to the range to break it in. How much ammo are you going to put through it before you feel comfortable carrying it?
How many rounds do you fire through your new CCW gun before you start carrying it?

Yea, I agree with running 2-300 rounds or until I am comfortable that it is reliable. I also shoot 10-15 rounds of various defence ammo I am thinking of carrying in it. I found that my Shield liked Critical Defence better than Gold Dot.

My buddy just got a new carry for his wife and it jammed a lot in the first 100 rounds, very few from 100-200 and none after 200. Looking at the manual, it said the gun had a break in period of 200 rounds so that made sense.
Couldn't say how many rds I fired thru my ccw however I didn't carry it until I was comfortable with it.
I first open with 200 rounds of Blazer Brass. Cheap and not good I know. Then I go onto my dirty ass weapon with Hornady Critical Duty, 25-50. Then I feel its good after a nice cleaning of course.

At the least, 500 without cleaning unless it absolutley can not live without a quick toothbrush down but now wet cleaning. I do not mean just blasting away through 500 rounds either.

This is just my own personal thinking. With in 500 rounds a gun has a chance to really shake it self or settle itself into its parts. The springs have been worked and the most of the inevitable machining burrs are knocked down. Just as important those 500 rounds allows a shooter to learn the character of the pistol or rifle. The shooter also learns the best manner in which to operate the gun by learning its greatness and shortcomings.

Lastly those 500 rounds allows ME to run any number of different ammo. That includes at least 2 weights for aluminum case, steel case, budget and foreign brass as well as domestic premium brass and of course at least 2 different reload recipes of my own.

The gun breaking in the shooter is just as important as the shooter breaking in the gun, to me anyways.

Ok so here is my newest obsession/set up. Zink Mini Splatling and Gear Combo

This build uses a lot of ink. The Mini Splatling is also the gun with the highest mobility in the game. So if you looked at the screen shot you can see this build is heaviest in Ink Recovery Up, with a total of a primary stat and 6 secondary stats in Ink Recovery. Followed by two primary stats in Run Speed, and working toward 3 minors in Ink Reducer Sub.

Every shot of the mini splatling fires what I call a "lick" you can see in the right hand side of the screen. Each lick is accompanied by 1 to 2 droplets of paint, randomly scattered between you and the distance your lick travelled. Using the guns mobility with high fire rate it's easy to cover a decent area or put a field of paint between you and another person just by strafing.

Adjusting your aim instead of/along with strafing can cover a larger area, using the range of your paint licks you can create much wider triangle type paint field between multiple enemies.

This build can be fun if you're a good shot and practice fighting at the weapons max distance. With the move speed and huge area the gun can paint it's very easy to fill your special, get into the nearest gun fight, kill them and bubble if you have to, then run off and paint up another special, repeat until victory.

People will try to be crafty. Hiding around corners, or just out of distance in their paint where you can see. Maybe they have Ninja Squid or Cold-Blooded, I don't know, things get crazy. That's where your disruptor comes in. And you can throw a lot of them with the ink refill you have. The disruptor, while being amazing for the fact it slows people to a crawl on foot or swimming, and reduces their ink recover, also puts a visible graphic on the enemy player. A small purple ring that pulses that can be seen above and below ink. This allows you to visibly see ninja squid, people slow swimming, or just check areas that are quiet.... too quiet.
